offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine of Rs.10,000/-
physical_harm: Deceased succumbed to injuries; PW 1 suffered injuries
premeditation_planning: Common intention to kill arose on the spur of the moment
motive: Stopping the deceased and others from contesting the College elections
key_evidence_accepted: Medical evidence corroborated by testimonies of the prosecution witnesses proved that the deceased died a homicidal death.
witness_credibility: Testimonies of the prosecution witnesses are fully reliable and there has been no improvement made. The testimony of an injured eye witness has to be given much credence.

legal_representation.accused: K. T. S. Tulsi, R. S. Suri, A. Sharan, Nagendra Rai, Y. Prabhakar Rao, Rahul Malhotra, Avinash Kumar, Chanchal Kumar Ganguli, Ms. Aprajita Mukherjee, Umang Shankar, M. C. Dhingra, Rajesh Sachdeva
legal_representation.state: Aditya Singh, Jatinder Kumar Bhatia, Jatinder Kumar Sethi, Umesh Arora, Prem Prakash, Gaurav Agrawal (AC), Dr. Abhishek Atrey, Ashutosh Kr. Sharma, Sumit Rajora

procedural_irregularity: Non-recovery of weapon used by accused, blood-stained shirt recovered after six days

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Sections 302 and 149 of the IPC

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons, armed with weapons, asked the victim and PW 1 to withdraw their names from the college election. On refusal, they assaulted the victim, leading to his death. The medical evidence and testimonies of the prosecution witnesses corroborated that the deceased died a homicidal death. The presence and participation of all accused in the offence were established, and the common intention to kill might have arisen on the spur of the moment.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was an improvement by the prosecution witnesses with respect to the place of occurrence of the incident. They also questioned the credibility of the prosecution witnesses, the medical evidence, and the absence of a common object of killing. The counsel for the appellants submitted that the prosecution story was unbelievable and that the deceased could have died due to falling on the ground.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the common object of an unlawful assembly may form on the spur of the moment, and the common intention to kill might have arisen at that time. The Court also emphasized that the testimony of an injured eye witness should be given much credence when supported by medical evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: Dharmendrasinh alias Mansing Ratansinh Vs. State of Gujarat (2002) 4 SCC 679; Manjit Singh and Anr. Vs. State of Punjab and Anr. (2013) 12 SCC 746; Ramachandran and Ors. Vs. State of Kerala (2011) 9 SCC 257
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution case was corroborated by medical evidence and the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses. The Court upheld the conviction and sentence of the accused persons under Sections 302 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code.
